title: MATH GAOKAO - 335
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Find the median of an unordered data set with an odd number of observations.
questions.question: Find the median of the data set \(7, 3, 9, 4, 7, 8, 6\).
questions.explanation:
Arrange the data in increasing order:
\[
3, 4, 6, 7, 7, 8, 9
\]
There are \(7\) observations, so the median is the \(4\)th value. The \(4\)th value is \(7\). Therefore, the median is \(7\).
questions.hint: First arrange the observations in increasing order, then locate the middle value.

questions.concept: Finding a Missing Value from the Median
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing data value when the median of a five-value data set is given.
questions.question: The data set \(4, 8, x, 10, 14\) has median \(9\). Find \(x\).
questions.explanation: For five observations, the median is the third value after arranging the data in increasing order. Since the median is \(9\), the third value must be \(9\). The value \(9\) lies between \(8\) and \(10\), so \(x=9\).
questions.hint: For five ordered observations, the median is the third value.

questions.concept: Median of an Even Number of Observations
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the median of an even-sized data set by averaging the two middle values.
questions.question: Find the median of the data set \(12, 15, 18, 20, 25, 31\).
questions.explanation:
The data are already in increasing order. There are \(6\) observations, so the median is the average of the \(3\)rd and \(4\)th values:
\[
\frac{18+20}{2}=19
\]
Therefore, the median is \(19\).
questions.hint: When the number of observations is even, average the two middle values after ordering the data.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the median from a small frequency distribution.
questions.question:
The table shows values and frequencies.
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\text{Value} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\
\hline
\text{Frequency} & 2 & 3 & 4 & 1
\end{array}
\]
Find the median.
questions.explanation:
The total frequency is \(2+3+4+1=10\). The median is the average of the \(5\)th and \(6\)th ordered values.
Cumulative frequencies:
\[
1:2,\quad 2:5,\quad 3:9,\quad 4:10
\]
The \(5\)th value is \(2\), and the \(6\)th value is \(3\). Hence the median is
\[
\frac{2+3}{2}=2.5
\]
questions.hint: Use cumulative frequencies to locate the positions of the middle values.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the median of an even-sized data set that contains repeated values.
questions.question: Find the median of the data set \(5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8\).
questions.explanation:
The data are already in increasing order. There are \(6\) observations, so the median is the average of the \(3\)rd and \(4\)th values:
\[
\frac{6+7}{2}=6.5
\]
Therefore, the median is \(6.5\).
questions.hint: Identify the two middle values after confirming the data are ordered.

questions.learningObjective: Estimate the median from a grouped frequency distribution using the median-class formula.
questions.question:
For the grouped data below, estimate the median.
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\text{Class} & [0,10) & [10,20) & [20,30) & [30,40) \\
\hline
\text{Frequency} & 4 & 6 & 10 & 5
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation:
The total frequency is \(N=4+6+10+5=25\), so \(N/2=12.5\).
Cumulative frequencies:
\[
[0,10):4,\quad [10,20):10,\quad [20,30):20,\quad [30,40):25
\]
The median class is \([20,30)\). Using the median formula
\[
\text{Median}=L+\frac{\frac{N}{2}-CF}{f}w
\]
with \(L=20\), \(CF=10\), \(f=10\), and \(w=10\), we get
\[
\text{Median}=20+\frac{12.5-10}{10}\cdot 10=20+2.5=22.5
\]
questions.hint: Locate the median class using cumulative frequencies, then apply the grouped median formula.

questions.concept: Missing Value from an Even-Sized Median
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value in an even-sized data set when the median is known.
questions.question: The data set \(3, 6, 9, x, 15, 18\) has median \(11\). Find \(x\).
questions.explanation:
There are \(6\) observations, so the median is the average of the \(3\)rd and \(4\)th ordered values. Since the median is \(11\), we need
\[
\frac{9+x}{2}=11
\]
Solving gives
\[
9+x=22 \implies x=13
\]
Thus \(x=13\).
questions.hint: For six ordered observations, the median is the average of the third and fourth values.

questions.concept: Effect of Linear Transformation on the Median
questions.learningObjective: Determine how an increasing linear transformation changes the median.
questions.question: The median of a data set \(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n\) is \(m\). If each observation is transformed to \(y_i=3x_i-2\), what is the median of the new data set?
questions.explanation:
The transformation \(y=3x-2\) is increasing because the coefficient \(3\) is positive. Therefore, the order of the observations is preserved, and the median is transformed in the same way as each observation. Hence the new median is
\[
3m-2
\]
questions.hint: An increasing linear transformation preserves the position of the median.

questions.concept: Median Change after Adding an Observation
questions.learningObjective: Use a change in the median to determine an original data value.
questions.question: The median of \(5\) observations is \(20\). A new observation \(30\) is added, and the median of the resulting \(6\) observations becomes \(22\). What is the fourth smallest value among the original \(5\) observations?
questions.explanation:
Let the original ordered observations be
\[
a_1\le a_2\le a_3\le a_4\le a_5
\]
Since the median of the original \(5\) observations is \(20\), we have \(a_3=20\).
After adding \(30\), there are \(6\) observations. The median is the average of the \(3\)rd and \(4\)th ordered values. The new median is \(22\), so
\[
\frac{a_3+a_4}{2}=22
\]
Substitute \(a_3=20\):
\[
\frac{20+a_4}{2}=22
\]
Thus
\[
20+a_4=44 \implies a_4=24
\]
Therefore, the fourth smallest original value is \(24\).
questions.hint: After adding the new observation, use the fact that the median of six values is the average of the third and fourth ordered values.

questions.learningObjective: Find the median of a combined data set from two small groups.
questions.question: Class A has scores \(60, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90\). Class B has scores \(65, 70, 75, 95\). Find the median of all \(10\) scores combined.
questions.explanation:
Combine and order all scores:
\[
60, 65, 70, 70, 75, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95
\]
There are \(10\) scores, so the median is the average of the \(5\)th and \(6\)th values:
\[
\frac{75+75}{2}=75
\]
Therefore, the median of the combined scores is \(75\).
questions.hint: Combine both classes, arrange all scores in increasing order, then average the two middle values.
